release_summary.summary: The requester (SH-CS) framed the problem as "tickets doubled since August, build an AI agent that auto-answers disputes and fixes wrong bills" (CL-01), but this was treated as a hypothesis, not the confirmed problem. The established root problem (PD-1): dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month in Jun/Jul to 1180-1260/month in Aug/Sep (E-04), and the majority (59%, 1785 of 3025) of disputed bills carried an ACTUAL meter read, not an ESTIMATED one (E-02) - meaning the error is mostly in how actual reads are billed, not in read collection. Tariff change was ruled out (E-01, E-06) and ticket response times are within SLA (E-03), so the originally-requested "faster AI answering" solution would not help. For the smaller ESTIMATED-read segment (1240 of 3025), mdms-export data (E-12) shows most estimate substitutions stem from a billing-import rule rejecting valid high-consumption AMI reads, not AMI/field delivery failure. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with nothing on hold. Only the completed field-completion cross-reference work item (cross_reference_field_completion_disputes:DA-ROUTE) was placed in release scope; investigating the billing rule change (DA-RULES) and pursuing MDMS vendor access were held out because two BEFORE_RELEASE verification obligations (VOB-U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRME, VOB-R-2) remain OPEN. The majority ACTUAL-read driver of the surge (1785 of 3025 disputes) is therefore not addressed by anything released. No automated bill-write capability exists or was authorized (K-BILLWRITE requires manual Billing Operations action), so the originally requested auto-fix agent is explicitly not supported.
key_points: Requester's framing (CL-01, SH-CS): build an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix wrong bills - this was treated as an unverified claim, not an accepted solution.

For the smaller ESTIMATED-read segment (1240 of 3025), mdms-export data (E-12) shows 1184 cases were valid AMI reads rejected by a billing-import high-consumption rule, versus only 56 true non-delivery cases - pointing to a billing-import rule issue, not AMI/field failure.
The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs).

The originally requested AI auto-answer/auto-fix agent is not supported: response times already meet SLA (E-03), so faster answering would not cut ticket volume, and automated bill writes are forbidden by K-BILLWRITE.

Tariff change was ruled out (E-01, E-06) and ticket response times are within SLA (E-03), so the originally-requested "faster AI answering" solution would not help. For the smaller ESTIMATED-read segment (1240 of 3025), mdms-export data (E-12) shows most estimate substitutions stem from a billing-import rule rejecting valid high-consumption AMI reads, not AMI/field delivery failure. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with nothing on hold. Only the completed field-completion cross-reference work item (cross_reference_field_completion_disputes:DA-ROUTE) was placed in release scope; investigating the billing rule change (DA-RULES) and pursuing MDMS vendor access were held out because two BEFORE_RELEASE verification obligations (VOB-U-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRME, VOB-R-2) remain OPEN. The majority ACTUAL-read driver of the surge (1785 of 3025 disputes) is therefore not addressed by anything released. No automated bill-write capability exists or was authorized (K-BILLWRITE requires manual Billing Operations action), so the originally requested auto-fix agent is explicitly not supported.

For the smaller ESTIMATED-read segment (1240 of 3025), mdms-export data (E-12) shows 1184 cases were valid AMI reads rejected by a billing-import high-consumption rule, versus only 56 true non-delivery cases - pointing to a billing-import rule issue, not AMI/field failure.

limitations_explained: No automated bill-adjustment capability exists in this release; any bill correction must be made manually by Billing Operations under K-BILLWRITE.

The originally requested AI auto-answer/auto-fix agent is not supported: response times already meet SLA (E-03), so faster answering would not cut ticket volume, and automated bill writes are forbidden by K-BILLWRITE.
